chunks: He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Malik al-Nahwi recited to me, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Ma'mooni recited to me, saying: My father recited to me, verses by al-Ma'mun:

"Protect yourself from things you loathe, by patience, for perhaps there may come a day when you will not see what you detest. How often a young man remains hidden while eyes vie to catch a glimpse of him, yet he is concealed. How often a literate man spares his tongue fearing the answer, yet he is truly eloquent. How often a dignified man smiles through harm, while his heart groans from its burning."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his pure progeny.

key_terms.العزاء: Al-'aza' — patience, consolation, endurance in the face of hardship
key_terms.الوقور: Al-waqur — the dignified, composed person who conceals inner suffering
key_terms.مفوه: Mufawwah — eloquent, gifted in speech despite choosing silence
key_terms.مموه: Mumawwah — concealed, disguised; one whose true worth is hidden

ai.seo_question: What poetry did the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun write about patience and dignity?
ai.summary: These are four lines of Arabic poetry attributed to the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun (r. 198-218 AH/813-833 CE), transmitted through a literary chain of reciters. The verses counsel patience in adversity, the value of concealment and restraint, and the nobility of enduring pain with outward composure. They reflect the courtly literary tradition of adab poetry that combined moral wisdom with rhetorical elegance, a genre cherished in the intellectual circles al-Ma'mun famously patronized.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Malik al-Nahwi recited the following verses to me from Abu al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Ma’mooni, who said my father recited for me, verses by al-Mamoon:

"Protect yourself from things you loathe, by patience, for perchance, there may be a day when you will not see anything you detest; Many a times, a man remains hidden, while eyes vie to have a sight of him; but he is concealed; Many a times, a literate man spares his tongue fearing the answer, and that silence becomes eloquent; Many a times, a dignified man smiles in pain, While his heart groans with its burn."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his pure progeny.
